title: A gate's own cargo, recreating target/ through a temporary target<random> sibling in the worktree root, fences the gate's credit as an outside worktree write
outcome: A gate whose own cargo process creates target/ (after a `cargo clean` or in a fresh worktree) is not fenced by cargo's temporary sibling directory, target<random>, in the worktree root. The workspace watcher treats that sibling as build output, the same as target/, so the gate earns its credit. A genuine outside write in the worktree still fences it.
acceptance: The workspace watcher treats cargo's temporary target-directory sibling at a worktree root (the name `target` followed by cargo's random suffix, created while cargo makes target/) as build output that does not fence a carried check, matching only cargo's exact naming so that other user files whose names start with 'target' still fence.

A fail-first test shows a carried check is not fenced by a change under such a sibling at the worktree root, while it is still fenced by a change to an ordinary file named like 'targets.txt' or 'target-notes.md' in the same worktree.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
